noCard.stepsTitle: 4 Simple Steps to Get Your Soil Tested:
noCard.step1Desc: Clear top debris from 8–10 spots across your field. Dig a 15 cm deep V-shaped hole with a spade. Thoroughly mix the soil from all spots, dry in the shade, and pack 500g in a clean bag.
noCard.step2Desc: Bring the sample to your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or block agriculture office.
noCard.step3Desc: Provide farmer name, mobile number, village, survey/gat number, farm size, and irrigation facility (well/borewell/canal/rainfed).
noCard.step4Desc: Once testing is complete, the laboratory issues your official report with nutrient levels and recommended fertilizer dosages.
noCard.govtTitle: Once You Receive Your Soil Health Card
noCard.govtStep1: 1. Obtain your official soil test report or Soil Health Card.
noCard.govtStep2: 2. If available digitally, download the PDF card from the government portal.
noCard.govtStep4: 4. Upload the report file or take a clear photo.
noCard.govtStep5: 5. FasalSaathi will read the values and explain recommendations in simple terms.
noCard.officialDisclaimer: Official laboratory testing is conducted exclusively by government/recognized soil testing centres.

cropDetail.phosphorusGood: Phosphorus is adequate for strong root development

cropDetail.potassiumGood: Potassium level is sufficient for disease resistance and grain quality
cropDetail.potassiumLow: Potassium is low; consider MOP (Muriate of Potash)
cropDetail.organicCarbonGood: Organic Carbon is adequate for microbial activity and water retention
cropDetail.organicCarbonLow: Organic Carbon is low; add farmyard manure (FYM) or green manure
